sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: The latest arXiv biology and biomedical announcement batch is Tuesday, 17 November 2026. From 27 deduplicated new-submission entries in the configured category listings, this report selects seven notable papers; the strongest pattern is data-efficient protein and transcriptome modelling, with complementary MRI measurement methods. Spoken agenda: antibody developability, RNA-based endpoint prediction, then imaging and mechanistic models. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking from incomplete biomedical coverage, not a popularity ranking. Snapshot: 2026-11-17T17:19:11Z; the current batch is used, not a prior batch.

sections.title: Multi-Assay Antibody Developability Prediction with Shared Structure-Language Representations
sections.abstract: MADM combines per-residue physicochemical descriptors, protein-language-model embeddings and shared multi-assay learning to predict antibody developability measurements.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports that structural descriptors match or exceed sequence-language embeddings on some assays; combining streams gives small consistent gains, and sharing training across correlated assays improves some correlations by about 0.1.
sections.unique_caveat: Several assay results are weaker and vary across data sources; the 80-antibody holdout loses about 0.1 Spearman correlation for most assays. This is retrospective model evaluation, not prospective antibody discovery validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New q-bio.BM listing; evaluated across eight assays assembled from 29 sources, with cluster-split tests and separate antibody panels.

sections.title: In-context learning predicts clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms
sections.abstract: PRTS uses labelled samples as context to predict diverse endpoints from bulk RNA-seq without per-cohort model training.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report the highest mean accuracy among tested methods, narrowly ahead of TabPFN v3.5; the advantage is mainly within cohorts, while performance across cohorts and unseen sites is comparable to the strongest baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: These are retrospective public-data benchmarks, not prospective clinical validation. The paper itself reports that the advantage does not persist across cohorts or unseen sites.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New genomics listing; evaluated on 175 held-out tasks and 44 TCGA tasks after pretraining on 6.0 million generated tasks; weights, code and a 1,160-cohort resource are reported as released.

sections.title: Multi-echo AxCaliberSMT: Mapping effective axon radius from restricted diffusion and radius-dependent intra-axonal T2
sections.abstract: ME-AxCaliberSMT combines diffusion and relaxation MRI contrasts to estimate effective axon radii across a broader size range than diffusion-only modelling.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that combining the two contrasts improved simulated radius accuracy and reproduced bundle-wise patterns on a commercial-gradient scanner, although absolute estimates differed by scanner.
sections.unique_caveat: The in-vivo sample is small; the authors note no histological validation or same-scanner scan-rescan data, simplifying straight-cylinder assumptions, and 66–68 minute protocols. Estimates remain model- and protocol-dependent.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New medical-physics listing; tested in simulations and in five healthy adults, four scanned on a second scanner. The paper reports mean cross-scanner bundle correlation of 0.73.

sections.title: Dynamic infrared thermography and computed tomography angiography fusion for DIEP flap perforator selection: a novel measurement system
sections.abstract: A workflow aligns dynamic infrared thermography hotspots with CTA-mapped perforators to combine functional perfusion signals with anatomy in DIEP flap planning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report linking 39 of 46 CTA perforators to thermal hotspots (84.8%) at a median offset of 14.74 mm, using automated one-to-one assignment to reduce subjective matching.
sections.unique_caveat: Only 12 patients were studied; 76.1% of detected hotspots had no CTA match, and the authors call for larger cohorts and surface validation. This validates a measurement workflow, not improved surgical outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New medical-physics listing; evaluated in 12 patients against 46 CTA perforators, and the arXiv record cites a 2026 IEEE Medical Measurements & Applications paper.

sections.title: From the possible to the optimal: differentiable optimization of gene regulatory networks
sections.abstract: jaxgrn combines differentiable programming with stochastic gene-network simulations to optimize ensembles of regulatory architectures for specified functions.
sections.claimed_contribution: In a morphogen-driven embryonic-patterning model, the authors report that constraints reshape which regulatory architectures support domain formation or positional information; imposing scaling narrows the solutions in some tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a computational study of a specified model, not experimental evidence that the inferred architectures occur or function in embryos.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New molecular-networks listing, cross-listed in quantitative biology; the authors optimize thousands of networks under varying noise, precision and scaling constraints.

sections.title: Generation of protein conformations using a simple inverted transformer
sections.abstract: A Transformer variant trained on one protein’s all-atom molecular-dynamics conformations is used to generate a weighted ensemble of protein structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports that generated conformations resemble sampled and experimental structures and quickly concentrate in highly populated regions of the studied protein’s conformational landscape.
sections.unique_caveat: Training and evaluation focus on a particular protein and its MD-derived data. The results do not establish transfer to other proteins or accurate thermodynamic sampling generally.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New quantitative-biology listing, cross-listed in biomolecules; the authors compare generated conformations with molecular-dynamics and experimental structures.

sections.title: An Exploration of Physical and Chemical Representation in Coarse-Grained, Machine-Learned Protein Models
sections.abstract: The authors compare seven coarse-graining maps to test how spatial resolution and chemical diversity affect system-specific learned protein models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that finer resolution and greater chemical diversity do not automatically improve accuracy; sufficiently expressive latent representations can support accurate protein-specific models with fewer chemical bead types.
sections.unique_caveat: The results concern system-specific models and the tested mapping choices; broader transfer across proteins and independent experimental validation are not established by the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New biomolecules listing, cross-listed in biological physics; the comparison varies both bead resolution and embedding type in learned coarse-grained models.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Protein developability and representation learning: MADM, the inverted Transformer and coarse-grained model comparison address distinct aspects of antibody properties or protein conformational modelling. Their validation differs—assay-labelled antibody data versus model-generated conformations—so the cluster is a snapshot, not evidence of a field-wide shift. Learning biological function from molecular data or models: PRTS predicts endpoints from bulk transcriptomes, while jaxgrn searches regulatory-network architectures in simulation. One is retrospective prediction and the other in-silico mechanism exploration; neither alone demonstrates prospective biological or clinical utility. Imaging and measurement methods: ME-AxCaliberSMT estimates white-matter microstructure and the DIRT–CTA workflow maps perforators. Both include human data, but small cohorts and measurement-level endpoints limit conclusions about clinical utility.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Antibody assay transfer: the MADM paper reports weaker performance and source variation for some assays. A useful follow-up would prospectively test a blinded, diverse antibody panel across laboratories using harmonized protocols, then separate sequence novelty from assay-source effects. Transcriptome model generalization: PRTS’s lead is strongest within cohorts and narrows across cohorts or sites. Independent prospective cohorts with locked endpoints, platform-stratified evaluation and external-site holdouts would test whether its contextual advantage transfers. MRI measurement validity: ME-AxCaliberSMT authors identify a small cohort, no scan-rescan or histological validation, and long acquisition time. Larger same-scanner repeat scans, matched histology where feasible, and optimized protocols could test reproducibility and model assumptions. From models to biology: jaxgrn and the protein-conformation Transformer derive results from computational systems. Follow-ups could compare prespecified regulatory architectures with perturbation experiments and test the conformation model on held-out proteins using independent structural and kinetic measurements. Surgical imaging evaluation: the DIRT–CTA paper reports a small cohort and many unmatched thermal hotspots. Multisite cohorts, threshold sensitivity analysis and intraoperative surface validation could assess matching reliability before evaluating effects on surgical decisions.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: This batch combines antibody-assay prediction and transcriptome-based endpoint modelling with two protein-structure methods, a gene-network optimizer and small-cohort MRI measurement studies. The most concrete evidence comes from assay-labelled benchmarks and human imaging feasibility data, but transfer and clinical utility remain open. Treat the ranking as relevance-based, not a measure of popularity or practice-changing evidence.
